name: EPA ECHO SOBE, Navajo Nation permits (prefix NN)
waters_covered: Window Rock, Kayenta, Tuba City, Twin Arrows, Shiprock, Chinle systems; Black Creek Wash, Moenkopi Wash, Laguna Creek, Nazlini Wash, San Juan River
access_detail: Daily ECHO ZIP filtered to permit_identifier LIKE 'NN%'. Sample research/tribal/raw/sobe-sample.json.

sample_record.sewer_overflow_bypass_description_text: Sewer line break in the wash behind school.

cannot_fill: published_at (no per-row publication time; daily file)
status_reason: 56 dated events from 6 NTUA permits with points, start, end and volume; the only dated overflow record for tribal lands in the West.
notes: By permit: NN0021555 Window Rock 24, NN0020281 Kayenta 14, NN0020290 Tuba City 9, NN0030344 Twin Arrows 4, NN0020621 Shiprock 3, NN0020265 Chinle 2. Many bypasses go 'into emergency lagoon' rather than to a water. Cross-check: the Tuba City overflow to Moenkopi Wash announced by the Navajo Nation (reported 2026-02-27) is in SOBE (start 2026-02-26 19:30, end 2026-02-28 03:30, 265,000 gallons, received 2026-03-04).

name: EPA SOBE collection-system registry, tribal-government owners (all regions)
access_detail: collection_system_permits.csv, owner type TRB, joined to the events table. Extract: research/tribal/raw/sobe-tribal-collection-systems.json.
status_reason: 84 tribal-owned collection systems are registered; only 9 have filed events (6 Navajo, Eastern Band of Cherokee NC0052469 with 6, Mississippi Band of Choctaw MS0043478/MS0043494 with 3).
notes: Registered with zero events include Region 10 (Lummi, Tulalip, Swinomish, Quinault, Makah, Yakama, Nez Perce, Warm Springs), Region 8 tribal lagoon general permits (NDG589..., SDG589..., WYG589101), Region 9 Arizona and California tribal systems, St. Regis Mohawk (SR0240281). Zero may mean no overflows or no filing; not distinguishable.

name: NTUA Sanitary Sewer Overflow Response Plan (Chinle, Kayenta and Tuba City), public notification section
legal_basis: Required by the EPA NPDES permits (SSO response plan condition)
status_reason: States NTUA's own public notification methods: website and Facebook, KTNN radio, door hangers, flyers, warning signs; timing set by NTUA with NNEPA.
notes: Quote: 'The reported SSO will be placed on NTUA's website and Facebook page.' 'If the SSO is severe enough to do public harm, it will be announced on KTNN radio ... or with door-to-door knocks or placement of door hangers.' Minimum content: 'information that an SSO has occurred, date, duration if known, estimated volume if known, location ... anticipated direction of the SSO, cause(s), the potential for harm ... and steps NTUA is taking'. Regulators (EPA Region 9, NNEPA) by phone within 24 hours. Major spill: over 1,000 gallons, or over 50 gallons near habitation or reaching public waters.

name: NTUA website and Facebook SSO postings
status_reason: The plan says SSOs are posted to NTUA's website and Facebook; no SSO list or news page was found on the website (Adobe Muse site; /news.html 404). Facebook not checked (no login).

name: Office of the President and Vice President of the Navajo Nation news releases (public health advisories for wastewater overflows)
operator: Navajo Nation Office of the President and Vice President
status_reason: Announced the Tuba City overflow advisory on Moenkopi Wash and its lifting (2026-03-06; release 2026-03-12); occasional, press-release only.
notes: Advice quoted: residents downstream to 'avoid contact with the water and to keep pets and livestock away'.

name: EPA Region 9 order to NTUA (Shiprock lift station spill to the San Juan River), 2016-12-22
status_reason: Shows EPA's practice: public notice is ordered case by case ('notify the public of the spill'), not posted by EPA itself.

name: EPA Region 9 NPDES permits and fact sheets for NTUA plants (e.g. NN0020281 Kayenta, 2024)
status_reason: EPA states it 'has not delegated primary regulatory responsibility for administering the NPDES permitting program to the Navajo Nation EPA'; permits carry Region 9's standard SSO language for small utilities (prohibition, reporting, response plan).

name: EPA Region 10 NPDES permits for tribal plants (e.g. Lummi Kwina Road WA0026727, 2015): Emergency Response and Public Notification Plan
status_reason: Region 10's standard clause requires immediate public notice of any overflow, through a plan the permittee writes.
notes: Quote: 'The Permittee must immediately notify the public, health agencies and other affected entities (e.g., public water systems) of any overflow which the Permittee owns or has operational control ... in accordance with the notification procedures developed in accordance with Part II.C of this Permit.' Same plan requirement seen in search results for Makah (WA0023213), Spokane Wellpinit (WA0025704), Swinomish (WA0025062). Assumed to match across Region 10 tribal permits.

name: EPA Region 6 response to comments, City of Gallup NM0020672 (2025): no public notification requirement
status_reason: Upstream of Navajo land, EPA added 24-hour reporting to NNEPA for spills that threaten Navajo land or water but declined NMED's request for public notification.
notes: EPA response: 'There is currently no applicable federal or the state regulatory requirements of the public notification for this facility currently. However, the permittee is encouraged to develop a communication procedure or plan ... EPA does not change the permit condition at this time regarding this request.'

name: ECHO facility search 'Indian Country' flag (IndianCountryRows / p_ico)
status_reason: Identifies permits located in Indian Country across regions, which permit prefixes do not (only Navajo uses NN; Region 8 uses state-coded general permits xxG589xxx; Region 10 uses WA/ID/OR codes; St. Regis Mohawk SR).
notes: The ECHO CWA REST response carries an IndianCountryRows count; the filter was not exercised in this round.

name: EPA regional 'sewage spill' public notices
status_reason: No EPA practice of posting public notices of individual overflows was found; EPA receives reports (eRule) and issues press releases only for enforcement actions.
